subject.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload

question: Should restart-drain bypass capability be exposed through public plugin SDK queue APIs, or kept as a core-owned internal restart path?
rationale: This PR changes a public plugin-facing queue contract and a security-sensitive gateway-draining boundary; automation cannot safely decide whether plugin authors should receive an explicit bypass capability.

options.title: Keep Bypass Internal
options.body: Remove public enqueueInternal-style API exposure and implement the restart exception through core-owned runtime context or queue internals only.

options.title: Approve Public SDK Bypass
options.body: Treat the bypass as an intentional plugin contract, document/version it, and add compatibility and misuse tests before merge.

options.title: Pause For Durable Recovery
options.body: Close or pause this dirty branch in favor of the broader SQLite restart-recovery work if maintainers prefer durable replay over in-process drain plumbing.

recommendation.title: Keep Bypass Internal
recommendation.body: Remove public enqueueInternal-style API exposure and implement the restart exception through core-owned runtime context or queue internals only.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent followup queue lifecycle and plugin SDK documentation work make this the strongest available owner for choosing the queue/API boundary.
